column1: # Use of and debate on § 249 Abs. 3 BauGB (Länderöffnungsklausel
column2: deadline 31.12.2015) by Land. Summaries follow the wiki pages in 'source'; marker as the wiki marks the fact. Curated 13.10.2026.

column3: Bayern passed the Gesetz zur Änderung der Bayerischen Bauordnung of 17.11.2014 (GVBl 2014, 478), in force 21.11.2014, which made the privilege for wind turbines depend on a distance of 10 H (Art. 82 BayBO); it was the only Land to use § 249 Abs. 3 BauGB before 31.12.2015.

Wirtschaftsminister Sven Morlok announced on 11.07.2014 that Sachsen would use the clause 'zügig' for a Land-wide 10H rule, but the CDU/SPD Koalitionsvertrag after the election of 31.08.2014 rejects 'Starre Mindestabstandsregelungen', DIE LINKE Antrag 6/466 (10.12.2014) asked the government not to use the clause, and the deadline passed without a Saxon law.
No use or debate found in this research.

The government refused to use the clause; BVB/Freie Wähler motions of 29.04.2015 (statutory minimum distances) and 20.11.2015 (Bundesrat initiative to extend the deadline) and the Volksinitiative 'Rettet Brandenburg' (10H) were not turned into law, and on 29.02.2016 the Parlamentarischer Beratungsdienst found that Brandenburg could no longer use § 249 Abs. 3 BauGB.

The FDP Gesetzentwurf Drs 19/2070 (16.06.2015) proposed 10H in the Hessian building code and had a hearing on 03.12.2015; the wiki records it as not adopted, but the outcome is not verified.

Kleine Anfrage Drs 6/4411 (Johann-Georg Jaeger, GRÜNE; answer by letter of 03.09.2015) records a Volksinitiative for 10H and a parallel Volksbegehren for 2,000 m; the government answered that 10H would amount to 'einer pauschalen Höhenbegrenzung' and kept its 1,000 m planning distance (the Volksinitiative's own Drucksache was not checked).

The FDP Antrag Drs 17/1973 (16.09.2014) asked the Landesregierung to use the Länderöffnungsklausel and set a minimum distance of 'zehnfachen der Nabenhöhe (10H)' between wind turbines and housing; no Landesgesetz followed.
